text:
elena: Hey everyone — quick announcement :megaphone: We’re kicking off an Open Hackweek focused on community contributions. Two big things: 1) mentorship signups, 2) Maintainer Microgrants. Also shipping community-templates v0.3.0 today. Details below and links in the thread. :tada:

sam: Love this — congrats! Where’s the release notes/CHANGELOG?

elena: Release notes here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-templates/releases/tag/v0.3.0 — highlights: new eval-harness template, short-form deploy manifests, and a CONTRIBUTING template for maintainers.

luis: I can mentor infra + ci topics during hackweek, count me in.

maya: Quick Q — who can apply for the microgrants? Are they for maintainers only or also new contributors/projects?

elena: Great question. Microgrants are aimed at maintainers and small project leads (including new projects) who need a little runway — up to $2,000 USD per accepted project. We’ll prioritize projects that unblock production-readiness, better CI, or community onboarding. Full guidelines: https://docs.redwood.inference/community/microgrants (link)

kevin: Will the templates include example evals + startup prompts? Trying to prep a demo.

elena: Yes — v0.3 includes an eval-harness example and a tiny prompt-library with tests. The goal is to make it trivial to run a quick regression check on a new model.

pm_bot: Heads up: Community newsletter slot requested for this. Please approve if you want us to include project highlights.

elena: Yes please — I’ll ping a few maintainers to nominate showcases.

release-bot: Released: community-templates v0.3.0 by @elena — assets: tarball, changelog, license. https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-templates/releases/tag/v0.3.0

sam: Nice. How do people sign up to mentor / apply for a grant?

elena: Mentor signups + grant applications are one form (separate checkboxes): https://forms.gle/community-hackweek-signup — deadline: 2 weeks from now. Hackweek is scheduled for the week of Oct 4 (will share exact timezone schedule).

luis: Will there be travel funding or is it remote only?

elena: Remote-first. If in-person meetups surface we may consider small meetup stipends, but the microgrants are cash to the project/maintainer.

kevin: Any required CLA/license for grant recipients?
elena: Recipients need to accept the standard contributor agreement and choose a permissive license (Apache-2.0 or MIT) for template-derived code; we’ll handle paperwork before payment.

sam: :thumbsup: I’ll echo this in eng channel and our contributors doc.

maya: Thanks — this is awesome. Will you need lightning talk slots? I can present a quick how-to for maintainers.

elena: That would be perfect — adding you to the volunteer list.

release-bot: Note: the release includes a SECURITY.md update and a small doc about running local evals to catch regressions early.

elena: Thanks everyone. If you’re a maintainer and want to be featured in the newsletter, DM me. Otherwise please RT the release link and encourage applicants. :seedling:
